implied_expectations.method: 10-year FCFE/owner-cash-per-share reverse model using normalized owner cash of $23.0B and 1.90B diluted A-equivalent shares.
implied_expectations.interpretation: The price does not require a bull case, but it does require durable high-single-digit owner-cash-per-share growth and a premium terminal multiple. The market already recognizes much of Visa's quality and digital-payments durability.

bear.thesis: Regulatory/routing remedies reduce network economics, client incentives remain elevated, RTP/stablecoins take selected flows, and VAS growth normalizes sharply.

base.thesis: Consumer payments compound at high single digits, cross-border and commercial flows remain healthy, VAS grows faster than the core and buybacks support per-share growth without major regulatory impairment.

bull.thesis: Visa becomes an even broader trust, tokenization, stablecoin and agentic-commerce layer while VAS and money movement sustain double-digit growth and regulatory remedies remain manageable.

permanent_loss_case.description: A combination of antitrust remedies, routing openness, RTP/stablecoin disintermediation and weaker pricing power permanently reduces Visa's take-rate economics even though the company remains solvent.

notes: Values are decision ranges, not price targets. FCFE proxy already includes interest and therefore does not add a separate enterprise-value net-debt bridge. The largest model sensitivities are terminal multiple, long-run owner-cash-per-share growth and the economic impact of regulatory remedies.
